pending_tags.title: Bushy Brow (apodo de Rock Lee)
pending_tags.body: Apodo que Sasuke y Naruto dan a Rock Lee (S01E06, cues 381, 384, 419, 448, 538). Se ha traducido como «Cejotas» (aumentativo sobre «cejas», registro coloquial de España). Alternativas: «Cejas Pobladas», «Cejudo». Pendiente de contrastar con el doblaje/manga de España.

pending_tags.title: Ino Pig (apodo que Sakura da a Ino)
pending_tags.body: Sakura llama a Ino «Ino Pig» (S01E06, cue 591). Se ha traducido como «Ino-cerda», con el mismo esquema que el apodo de Sakura («Pista de Aterrizaje»). Pendiente de contrastar con el doblaje de España.

pending_tags.title: Rookie Nine (los nueve Genin novatos)
pending_tags.body: Kabuto llama «Rookie Nine» a los nueve Genin recién salidos de la Academia (S01E06, cue 618). Se ha traducido como «Nueve Novatos». Pendiente de decidir si se fija como término recurrente (aparecerá en episodios posteriores).

pending_tags.title: Leaf Whirlwind (técnica de Rock Lee)
pending_tags.body: Técnica de taijutsu de Rock Lee (S01E06, cue 392), de la que el inglés solo da «Leaf Whirlwind». Se ha traducido literalmente como «Torbellino de la Hoja». Pendiente de contrastar con el nombre en el manga Planeta / doblaje de España (Konoha Senpū).

pending_tags.title: Third Eye (técnica de Gaara)
pending_tags.body: Técnica de Gaara con la que observa el examen usando un ojo de arena (S01E06, cue 916). Se ha traducido como «Tercer Ojo». El inglés lo dice en cursiva y como pensamiento; se atribuye a Gaara por contexto. Pendiente de contrastar con el manga Planeta.

pending_tags.title: Paw Encyclopedia (S01E05)
pending_tags.body: English "Paw Encyclopedia", the book of cat paw prints Sasuke and Itachi compiled. Translated literally as "Enciclopedia de Patas". The official Spain rendering is unknown.

pending_tags.title: silvervine drink (S01E05)
pending_tags.body: English "silvervine drink" (the plant cats are drawn to, matatabi in Japanese). Kept as "bebida de matatabi" to preserve the cat-plant reference. Alternatives: "actinidia" or a plain "bebida para gatos".

pending_tags.title: vendetta (S01E05)
pending_tags.body: English "vendetta" / "vendetta permit" / "34 vendettas" for the legal revenge-killing arc. Kept as "vendetta" (common in Spain Spanish) with "permiso de vendetta". Alternative: "venganza" / "permiso de venganza".

pending_tags.title: Lock Village and Land of Key (S01E05)
pending_tags.body: English "Hidden Lock Village" in the "Land of Key", later shortened to "Lock Village" and "ninja of the Lock". Rendered "Aldea Oculta del Cerrojo", "País de la Llave", "Aldea del Cerrojo". The official village and country names are unverified (follows the "Aldea Oculta de la Hoja" pattern).

pending_tags.title: "Fire Style!" (S01E05)
pending_tags.body: Bare shout "Fire Style!" (no technique name). Rendered "¡Técnica ígnea!" to match the glossary entry "Técnica ígnea: Gran bola de fuego". Earlier episodes (S01E01-S01E04) render the same prefix as "Elemento Fuego", which conflicts with the glossary; both need reconciling.

pending_tags.title: Pachinko Jutsu (S01E05)
pending_tags.body: Combination attack named "Pachinko Jutsu" in the English. Rendered "Jutsu Pachinko". Unknown whether the Spanish edition transliterates or adapts it.

pending_tags.title: Expansion Jutsu (S01E05)
pending_tags.body: English "Expansion Jutsu" (Akimichi Multi-Size family). Rendered "Jutsu de Expansión". The glossary has "Multitamaño Parcial" and "Jutsu Super Multi Tamaño" for related techniques, so this may need to align with the "Multi Tamaño" family.

pending_tags.title: Hidden Jutsu: Beetle Sphere (S01E05)
pending_tags.body: English "Hidden Jutsu: Beetle Sphere" (Aburame technique). Rendered "Jutsu Secreto: Esfera de Escarabajos". Both the "Hidden Jutsu" prefix (secreto vs oculto) and the technique name are unverified.

pending_tags.title: Mind Transfer Jutsu (S01E05)
pending_tags.body: English "Mind Transfer Jutsu" (Yamanaka technique). Rendered "Jutsu de Transferencia de Mente". Unverified.

pending_tags.title: Heaven Scroll / Earth Scroll
pending_tags.body: "Heaven Scroll" and "Earth Scroll" rendered as "Pergamino del Cielo" and "Pergamino de la Tierra" (S01E07). Only the first occurrence is tagged; all later uses in the episode follow the same wording.

pending_tags.title: Fire Style: Phoenix Flower Jutsu
pending_tags.body: Rendered "Técnica ígnea: Flor de Fénix", following the glossary's "Técnica ígnea:" pattern. The glossary only has "Llamas del Fénix" for the Phoenix Sage Fire Jutsu, which is a different technique. Later uses in S01E07 use the same wording untagged.

pending_tags.title: Paper Bomb
pending_tags.body: "Paper Bomb" rendered "sello explosivo" (S01E07). Alternative: "papel bomba". Later uses in the episode use "sello explosivo" untagged.

pending_tags.title: "Ninja Art:" technique prefix
pending_tags.body: "Ninja Art:" rendered "Arte ninja:" before technique names (S01E07, Senbon Rainstorm rendered "Lluvia de Agujas", Shadow Possession and Mind Transfer also use the prefix). Only the first occurrence is tagged.

pending_tags.title: Sand Coffin / Sand Burial
pending_tags.body: "Sand Coffin" rendered "Ataúd de Arena" (tagged) and "Sand Burial" rendered "Funeral de Arena" (untagged, next cues).

pending_tags.title: Curse Mark / Five-Pronged Seal
pending_tags.body: "Five-Pronged Seal" rendered "Sello de Cinco Puntas" and "Curse Mark" rendered "Sello Maldito" (S01E07). The glossary has "Sello" conventions for other seals but not these.

pending_tags.title: Sound Village techniques and ninja
pending_tags.body: "Sound ninja" rendered "ninjas del Sonido" and "Sound Village" rendered "Aldea del Sonido" (tagged at the first use, cue 506). "Slicing Sound Wave" rendered "Onda Sonora Cortante" (tagged at first use, cue 787); "Super Sound Wave" as "Súper Onda Sonora" and "Super Sonic Slicing Wave" as "Onda Sonora Cortante Supersónica".

pending_tags.title: Striking Shadow Snakes
pending_tags.body: Rendered "Serpientes Sombra Golpeadoras" (S01E07, Anko's technique).

pending_tags.title: Leaf Hurricane
pending_tags.body: Rendered "Huracán de la Hoja" (S01E07, Lee). "Leaf Style Taijutsu" (Choji) rendered "Taijutsu Estilo Hoja", untagged.

pending_tags.title: Beautiful Green Beast of the Leaf
pending_tags.body: Lee's epithet rendered "la Bestia Verde de la Hoja", dropping "Beautiful" (S01E07). Also "Bushy Brow" rendered "Cejotas" (cue 995), untagged.

pending_tags.title: Primary Lotus
pending_tags.body: Rendered "Loto Primario" (S01E07, Lee).

pending_tags.title: Ino-Shika-Cho formation and Mind Transfer
pending_tags.body: "Formation Ino" rendered "Formación Ino" (tagged); "Expansion Jutsu" rendered "Jutsu de Expansión" and "Mind Transfer Jutsu" rendered "Jutsu de Transferencia de Mente" (untagged, S01E07). "Human Boulder" uses the verified glossary entry "Bola de Tanque Humano".

pending_tags.title: Shadow Clone Jutsu: Fishing Version

pending_tags.title: Pervy Sage (Jiraiya's nickname)
pending_tags.body: Naruto's recurring nickname for Jiraiya, "Pervy Sage" (S01E09, first use cue 451). Rendered "Senninfómano", the official Spanish nickname confirmed by the Planeta character guide (vol. 1, glossary entry: "Senninfómano: Es el mote que le puso Naruto a Jiraiya"), a portmanteau of "sennin" (sabio ermitaño) and "ninfómano". Only the first occurrence is tagged; used untagged throughout the rest of the episode. Strong source, but flagged since this is a high-frequency epithet that will recur in almost every future episode featuring Jiraiya and is worth confirming as the fixed project convention.

pending_tags.title: Closet Perv (Naruto's nickname for Ebisu)
pending_tags.body: Naruto calls Ebisu "The Closet Perv" / "Closet pervert" on first meeting him (S01E09, first use cue 233). Rendered "el Pervertido de Armario", a literal calque of the English "closet" (hidden/secret) metaphor. No official Spanish-dub or manga source found; the character guide only confirms "pervertido" as a listed personality trait for Ebisu, not this specific nickname. Only the first occurrence is tagged.

pending_tags.title: Great Toad Sage of Mount Myoboku
pending_tags.body: Jiraiya's mock self-introduction the first time Naruto meets him, "I am the Great Toad Sage of Mount Myoboku, the immortal... also known as the Toad Mountain Sage" (S01E09, cue 447-448). Rendered "el Sabio Sapo del Monte Myoboku" / "el Sabio Montaña Sapo". "Monte Myoboku" itself is confirmed by the Planeta character guide (recurring as "monte Myóboku"); the "Great Toad Sage" title is Jiraiya's own comedic exaggeration in-universe (not the same as "Ogama Sennin", the actual toad elder character named later in the guide) and has no direct official rendering.

pending_tags.title: One-Tail (Gaara's Tailed Beast, before "Shukaku" is named)
pending_tags.body: "The One-Tail" (S01E09, first use cue 688), referring to Gaara's Tailed Beast before the anime reveals its name (Shukaku). Rendered "el Ichibi", kept in Japanese rather than extending the glossary's numeric "Nine-Tails" -> "el Nueve Colas" pattern, because "el Uno Cola" / "el Un Cola" reads ungrammatically in Spanish for a singular tail. The character guide confirms "Shukaku, el espíritu de la arena" as the eventual name, but using it here would be a spoiler ahead of the anime's own reveal.

pending_tags.title: Playing Possum Jutsu
pending_tags.body: Baki describes Gaara's ability, "when the One-Tail transforms completely and activates his Playing Possum Jutsu, there's no stopping him" (S01E09, cue 695). Rendered "Técnica del Sueño Instantáneo", matching the Planeta character guide's description of Gaara's technique of inducing sleep to unleash Shukaku's full power ("una técnica de sueño... Técnica del sueño instantáneo" appears in the guide's technique index). The identification of "Playing Possum" with this guide technique is an interpretive judgment call, not a literal name match.

pending_tags.title: Eight Trigrams Sealing Style / Four-Symbols Seal
pending_tags.body: Jiraiya's internal analysis of Naruto's seal: "Two Four-Symbols Seals making up an Eight Trigrams Seal... So it's an Eight Trigrams Sealing Style" (S01E09, cue 602-603). Rendered "Sello de los Cuatro Símbolos" and "Sello/Estilo de Sellado de los Ocho Trigramas". No source found in the manga/guide database; literal translation of the English fansub terms (the seal's canonical Japanese name is Hakke no Fūin Shiki).
